title: Grateful Dead Live at Ivar Theater on 1966-02-25

ai_review.summary: An astonishing early‑'66 soundboard capture with crystal‑clear tape quality that showcases a raw, high‑energy set – Pigpen wailing, Jerry’s soaring solos and a legendary King Bee → Caution jam.
ai_review.review: The recording is a rare soundboard source from the spring of ’66 that sounds astonishingly clean for its era, with only a faint ribbon‑mic hiss on vocals. Musically the show is often described as “hot” and “primal,” highlighted by Pigpen’s bluesy harpsichord, Jerry Garcia’s killer leads (especially on I Know You Rider), and an unforgettable King Bee → Caution/​Schoolgirl jam that many fans rank among the best of the year.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 40 reviews uniformly award 5‑star ratings, praising both performance and tape fidelity; the consensus is that this is an exceptional early‑Dead show captured on a superb soundboard source.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, balanced mix with remarkable clarity for 1966; occasional ribbon‑mic hiss/distortion on Jerry’s vocal mic noted but not detrimental. No drop‑outs or tape glitches reported.

standout_songs: Schoolgirl > You Don't Love Me > Schoolgirl
show_quality.setlist_flow: Fans describe the set as a wild, experimental “petri‑dish” of early Dead – raw blues energy, tight transitions and an especially powerful middle jam that keeps the momentum soaring.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for fiery lead work, perfect tone, wailing solo on I Know You Rider and overall guitar brilliance.
band_member_comments.Phil: Noted for solid, driving bass lines; several reviewers call his playing “great” and essential to the groove.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann’s early mastery highlighted – tight, propulsive drumming that fuels the show.
